title: Handball: Fast-Paced Team Play
summary: How handball combines running, jumping, and throwing at speed, the basic rules and scoring, and the different jobs players do on the court.
poll: Jumping into the air to shoot is the most exciting part of handball.

versions.title: Fast Handball
versions.text:
Run. Jump. Throw hard. This is handball!

Two teams play on a court. Each team has a ball. You throw the ball at a net. That net is the goal.

You can run with the ball. But you can take just three steps. Then you must pass it. Or you can bounce it. Or you can throw it at the goal.

Near the goal, you jump up high. You throw while you are up in the air. This can trick the other team.

Each team has jobs. Some run fast on the sides. Some throw hard from far back. One player stays near the goal to help score.

The other team tries to stop you. They put their arms up. They block your throw.

Each goal is worth one point. The team with more points wins.

Handball makes you fast. It makes you strong. It helps you play as a team.

versions.text:
Running at full speed, leaping explosively, and throwing with real power: handball combines all three actions into one continuously fast-moving team sport.

Handball is a fast-paced sport played in schools and sports clubs throughout the world. Two teams of seven players, including one goalkeeper apiece, compete on a single indoor court, and each team's objective is to propel a ball past the opposing goalkeeper and into the net.

A player who gains possession of the ball is permitted to run with it, but for no more than three steps before doing something else with it. After three steps, that player must pass to a teammate, dribble by bouncing the ball repeatedly against the floor, or attempt a shot toward the goal.

Close to the goal, players frequently leap high into the air before releasing a shot, a technique that depends on straightforward physics. Because stepping inside the marked six-meter goal area is prohibited, an attacking player instead launches from outside that line, releases the ball while still airborne, and lands only after the ball has left their hand. As the player leaps, rotates the trunk explosively, and snaps the wrist forward at the final instant, the body's accumulated momentum transfers efficiently into the ball, generating considerable velocity and a steep, downward trajectory that a diving goalkeeper often cannot reach in time.

Each team organizes its seven players into specific tactical roles. Quick wing players sprint along the sides of the court, constantly searching for open space near the goal post and often finishing with sharply angled shots. Powerful back players unleash hard shots from farther out, where defenders generally have more room and time to react. One player, known as the pivot, positions themselves directly in front of the opposing goal, using their body to screen a defender and create space for a teammate to shoot.

The instant a team loses possession, all six of its court players must switch immediately into a defensive formation. Skilled defenders learn to anticipate an attacker's next move by reading subtle cues in the hips and shoulders, using their arms and bodies to block throws and step directly into the attacker's path, taking care never to push or hold an opponent, an infraction a referee would penalize as a foul.

Every successful shot counts as exactly one point, and a complete match is normally divided into two equal halves, each lasting roughly thirty minutes. Whichever team has accumulated more goals once the final whistle sounds is declared the winner.

Playing handball builds speed, strength, and stamina, since virtually every attacking sequence combines running, jumping, and throwing within just a few seconds. It also develops genuine teamwork and communication, because all seven players on the court must constantly cooperate, both while attacking and while defending.

Running at full sprint, leaping explosively into the air, and throwing with considerable accumulated power, built up through years of dedicated practice: handball combines all three of these physically demanding actions into one continuously fast-moving, highly dynamic team sport that challenges both body and mind.

Handball is a fast-paced sport played competitively in schools, clubs, and international tournaments, including the Olympic Games, throughout virtually every region of the world, from small towns to major cities. Two teams of seven players apiece, each including a single designated goalkeeper, compete simultaneously on one indoor court, and each team's fundamental objective, refined over more than a century of organized play, is to propel a ball past the opposing goalkeeper and into the net.

A player who gains possession of the ball is permitted to run with it, but for no more than three steps before doing something else with it, a restriction that forces constant decision-making under pressure. After three steps, that player must either pass to a teammate, dribble by repeatedly bouncing the ball against the floor, or attempt a shot directed toward the goal.

Close to the goal, players frequently leap explosively into the air before releasing a shot, a technique that fundamentally depends on genuinely straightforward principles of physics, principles that top athletes refine instinctively through years of repetition. Because stepping inside the marked six-meter goal area is strictly prohibited under the rules, an attacking player instead launches from outside that boundary line, releases the ball while still fully airborne, and lands only after the ball has already departed their hand. As the player leaps, rotates the trunk explosively, and snaps the wrist forward at precisely the final instant, the body's accumulated momentum transfers efficiently through the arm, functioning almost like a cracking whip, into the ball itself, generating considerable velocity together with a steep, downward trajectory that a diving goalkeeper frequently cannot reach in time, regardless of their reflexes or experience.

Each team organizes its seven players into clearly defined tactical roles, roles that coaches study and refine across an entire competitive season. Quick wing players sprint continuously along the sides of the court, constantly searching for open space near the goal post and frequently finishing with sharply angled shots. Powerful back players unleash forceful shots from considerably farther out, where defenders generally possess more room and time to react. One specialized player, known as the pivot, positions themselves directly in front of the opposing goal, using their body deliberately to screen a defender and create valuable space for a teammate to shoot.

The instant a team loses possession, all six of its court players must switch immediately into a coordinated defensive formation, a transition that elite teams practice until it becomes nearly automatic. Skilled defenders learn to anticipate an attacker's next move by carefully reading subtle cues in the hips, shoulders, and eyes, using their arms and bodies to block throws and step directly into the attacker's intended path, taking considerable care never to push or hold an opponent, an infraction that a referee would invariably penalize as a foul.

Every successful shot counts as exactly one point, and a complete match is normally divided into two equal halves, each lasting roughly thirty minutes, with a short break between them. Whichever team has accumulated more goals by the time the final whistle sounds is officially declared the winner of the match.

keyWords.example: The coach asked the tallest player on the team to play pivot near the goal.

keyWords.definition: a team's turn trying to move the ball forward and score
keyWords.example: During the attack, every player tried to find open space near the goal.

keyWords.definition: to move a ball by bouncing it again and again
keyWords.example: She can dribble the ball quickly down the court before passing it.

questions.stem: Which sentence best states the central idea of the article?
options: Success in handball depends only on a player's height
Handball is really just a slow, calm version of basketball
Handball mixes fast running, jumping, throwing, rules, and defense
Teams in handball try to score fewer points than rivals
questions.why: The article explains the three-step rule, the jump shot, team roles like wing and pivot, and how defenders try to stop each attack.

wrong.A: The article never says height decides success.
wrong.B: Handball is described as fast-paced, not slow or calm.
wrong.D: Teams try to score more goals than the other team, not fewer.

questions.stem: According to the article, what must a player do after taking three steps while holding the ball?
options: Pass to a teammate, dribble it, or shoot at the goal
Hand the ball directly over to the referee
Walk slowly off the court to the sideline
Wait quietly for the goalkeeper to approach the player
questions.why: The article says that after three steps, a player must pass, dribble, or shoot.

wrong.B: Giving the ball to the referee is not a rule in the article.
wrong.C: Walking to the sideline is not mentioned.
wrong.D: Waiting for the goalkeeper is not part of the rule.

questions.stem: What does the pivot mainly do for the team?
options: Blocks throws from far outside the court area
Stands near the goal and opens space for a teammate
Takes over as goalkeeper in the second half
Decides on their own which team wins the match
questions.why: The article says the pivot positions themselves near the opposing goal and uses their body to create space for a teammate.

wrong.A: Blocking from far away describes defenders, not the pivot's main job.
wrong.C: The pivot does not replace the goalkeeper.
wrong.D: Match results depend on goals scored, not on one player's decision.

questions.stem: Why do attacking players jump from outside the goal area instead of stepping inside it?
options: Stepping inside the goal area is against the rules, so players jump instead
Jumping simply feels more comfortable than shooting while standing still
The marked goal area is thought to be wet and slippery
Referees require that every shot involve a jump of some kind
questions.why: The article explains that stepping inside the marked goal area is against the rules, so players jump over it to shoot legally.

wrong.B: Comfort is not the reason given in the article.
wrong.C: The goal area being wet is not mentioned.
wrong.D: Not every shot requires a jump.

questions.stem: A defender pushes an attacking player to stop a shot. Based on the article, what will most likely happen?
options: The defending team is awarded an extra goal automatically
The referee will call a foul on the defender
The attacker must leave the court for the rest of the match
The whole match will end immediately after the push
questions.why: The article says defenders must be careful not to push or hold attackers, which the referee would call a foul.

wrong.A: Pushing does not reward the defending team with a free goal.
wrong.C: The article does not say the attacker must leave the match.
wrong.D: One foul does not end the match.

questions.stem: Why might back players often shoot from farther away than wing players do?
options: Defenders usually have more room and time to react near the goal
Back players are never allowed anywhere near the goal area
Shots from farther away are always easier for every player
The goalkeeper cannot see shots taken from far away
questions.why: The article explains that back players shoot from farther out partly because defenders have more room and time closer to the goal.

wrong.B: Back players are allowed near the goal; they simply often shoot from farther out.
wrong.C: The article does not claim distant shots are always easier.
wrong.D: The article does not say the goalkeeper cannot see far shots.

questions.stem: How is the article mainly organized?
options: As a timeline of one real match from the first kick to the final whistle
By explaining different parts of handball: rules, shots, roles, and defense
As a comparison between handball and a game of water polo in a pool
As step-by-step instructions for building a handball court at school
questions.why: Each part of the article explains a different piece of how handball works, from rules to roles to scoring.

wrong.A: No single match is described from start to finish.
wrong.C: Water polo is not mentioned.
wrong.D: Building a court is not explained.

questions.stem: Based on the article, how is a wing player different from a pivot?
options: A wing player stays still near the goal while the pivot runs along the sides
A wing player runs along the sides, while the pivot stands near the goal
A wing player never touches the ball, while the pivot always holds it
There is really no difference at all between these two roles
questions.why: The article describes wings as running along the sides of the court, while the pivot stays near the opposing goal.

wrong.A: This reverses the two roles described in the article.
wrong.C: Both roles involve handling the ball during play.
wrong.D: The article clearly separates these two roles.

MID.prompt: Imagine you are coaching a new handball team. Explain how possession changes between attack and defense, using at least two key words from the article.
checklist: I explained what happens when a team has possession.
I explained what happens when a team loses possession.
I used at least two key words correctly.
MID.modelAnswer: When a team has possession of the ball, it moves into attack, with the pivot creating space near the goal while wings and backs look for an open shot, often finishing with a dribble and a jump shot. The moment that team loses possession, every player must become a defender, blocking throws and stepping into the path of the other team's attack.

keyWords.definition: how fast something is moving in a certain direction
keyWords.example: The arrow left the bow with tremendous velocity.

keyWords.definition: the curved path an object follows as it moves through the air
keyWords.example: The rocket's trajectory curved far above the clouds before leveling off.

keyWords.definition: the force an object has because it is moving, which depends on its speed and mass
keyWords.example: The rolling boulder gained momentum as it sped down the steep hill.

keyWords.definition: to guess what will happen next and get ready for it
keyWords.example: A good goalkeeper learns to anticipate where a shot will go before it is released.

keyWords.definition: a particular way of doing something skillfully
keyWords.example: The diver used flawless technique to enter the water without a splash.

questions.stem: Which statement best expresses the central idea of the article?
options: Handball results depend mostly on luck, not on skill, strategy, or hard training
The jump shot, team roles, and defense all rely on technique and basic physics
Physics explains basketball far better than it explains handball or any other sport
Only the goalkeeper's actions decide a handball match's outcome in every game
questions.why: The article connects the jump shot, team roles, and defensive anticipation to physical technique and simple physics, not just speed.

wrong.A: The article credits skill, rules, and technique, not luck.
wrong.C: The article applies physics specifically to handball, not basketball.
wrong.D: Many players, not only the goalkeeper, affect the outcome.

questions.stem: According to the article, what happens to momentum as a player leaps, rotates the trunk, and snaps the wrist during a jump shot?
options: It disappears completely the instant the player leaves the ground
It only affects how the player lands, not the ball at all
It passes through the arm and gives the ball velocity and trajectory
It is cancelled out entirely by the defender's block before release
questions.why: The article explains that momentum transfers through the arm into the ball, generating velocity and a downward trajectory.

wrong.A: Momentum does not simply disappear during the jump.
wrong.B: The article focuses on how momentum affects the ball, not just the landing.
wrong.D: A block, if it happens, is separate from how momentum builds the shot.

questions.stem: According to the article, how do skilled defenders anticipate an attacker's next move?
options: By reading subtle cues in the attacker's hips, shoulders, and eyes
By asking the referee to reveal the attacker's plan in advance
By watching only the scoreboard throughout the match
By copying the exact movements made by their own goalkeeper
questions.why: The article states that skilled defenders anticipate an attacker's next move by reading cues in the hips, shoulders, and eyes.

wrong.B: Referees do not reveal a team's plans.
wrong.C: The scoreboard does not show a player's next move.
wrong.D: Defenders read the attacker, not the goalkeeper's movements.

questions.stem: Why does jumping before releasing a shot, instead of shooting from the ground, help an attacker create a steeper downward trajectory?
options: Jumping has no real effect on the ball's path at all
Jumping only helps a player avoid the goal area
Jumping always slows down the throw's speed
Releasing the ball higher lets momentum angle it downward
questions.why: Releasing the ball from a higher point while the body's momentum moves forward and downward creates a steeper, harder-to-stop trajectory.

wrong.A: The article links the jump directly to the ball's downward trajectory.
wrong.B: Legality is one reason for jumping, but the article also connects it to the shot's trajectory.
wrong.C: The article describes the jump shot as generating considerable velocity, not reducing it.

questions.stem: A defender fails to anticipate an attacker's next move and reacts a moment too late. Based on the article, what is the most likely result?
options: The attacker's shot is more likely to beat the block
The match is stopped at once for a time-out and a break
The attacker automatically loses the ball to the referee
The goalkeeper is removed from the game by the coach
questions.why: Since anticipation helps defenders block throws in time, reacting too late makes it more likely the shot gets through.

wrong.B: A late reaction does not stop the match.
wrong.C: A late defender does not cause the attacker to lose the ball.
wrong.D: The goalkeeper's status does not change because of a defender's timing.

questions.stem: Based on the article, how does the momentum behind an attacker's throw differ from a defender's attempt to anticipate and block it?
options: Both rely on the exact same physical motion and timing
Momentum only matters for defenders, not attackers
Momentum drives the ball; anticipation aids positioning
Anticipation equals generating momentum physically
questions.why: The attacker's momentum propels the ball, while a defender's anticipation is about timing and positioning, not generating force on the ball.

wrong.A: A throw and a defensive read involve different physical actions.
wrong.B: The article discusses momentum mainly in relation to the attacker's throw.
wrong.D: Anticipation is about reading cues, not building momentum.

questions.stem: The article says the jump shot is a technique that depends on physics. What does technique mean as it is used here?
options: A rule that is enforced only by the referee
A skillful way of acting, honed through practice
A penalty that is given whenever a foul happens
The official name for the goal area of the court
questions.why: Technique refers to the skillful, practiced way a player performs the jump shot.

wrong.A: Technique is a player's skill, not a referee's rule.
wrong.C: Technique is not a type of penalty.
wrong.D: Technique does not name a part of the court.

questions.stem: Why does the author explain the physics behind the jump shot and defensive anticipation in such detail?
options: Only scientists can truly enjoy handball
Handball is more dangerous than other sports
Handball compares unfavorably to basketball
Split-second actions follow real physical laws
questions.why: By explaining momentum, velocity, trajectory, and anticipation, the author shows that split-second handball actions have a physical explanation.

wrong.A: The explanation is meant for general readers, not only scientists.
wrong.B: Danger compared to other sports is not discussed.
wrong.C: Basketball is not compared in this article.

HIGH.prompt: Choose two ideas from the article, one about attacking and one about defending, and explain how each depends on physics or technique.
checklist: I explained one attacking idea and connected it to physics or technique.
I explained one defending idea and connected it to physics or technique.
I used precise vocabulary, including at least two key words.
HIGH.modelAnswer: On attack, a player's jump shot depends on momentum and technique: as the player leaps, rotates the trunk, and snaps the wrist, that momentum transfers into the ball, producing high velocity and a steep trajectory toward the goal. On defense, a skilled defender relies on the ability to anticipate the attacker's next move by reading small cues in the hips and shoulders, which lets the defender position their body in time to block the throw before it ever reaches full speed.

LOW.stem: Where do the players who throw hard stand?
options: Near the goal
Far back from the goal
Behind the other team
On the sides
LOW.why: The text says some players throw hard from far back.

wrong.A: One player stays near the goal to help score, not the hard throwers.
wrong.C: The text never says players stand behind the other team.
wrong.D: The players on the sides are the ones who run fast.

LOW.stem: How does the author begin the article?
options: With a short story
With a list of rules
With a question
With three action words
LOW.why: The article starts with the short action words Run, Jump, and Throw hard.

wrong.A: The article does not start with a story.
wrong.B: The rules come later, not at the start.
wrong.C: The first lines are not a question.

LOW.stem: In the article, what does the word block mean?
options: To stop something
To throw far
To count points
To jump high
LOW.why: The other team puts their arms up to stop the throw, so block means to stop.

wrong.B: Blocking is the opposite of throwing the ball far.
wrong.C: Counting points is not what the defenders do with their arms.
wrong.D: Jumping is what the thrower does near the goal.

LOW.stem: A player is very fast but not very strong. Which job fits her best?
options: Throwing from far back
Staying near the goal
Running fast on the sides
Standing still at the back
LOW.why: The text says some players run fast on the sides, so a fast player fits that job.

wrong.A: Throwing hard from far back needs a strong player.
wrong.B: The player near the goal helps score, not run fast.
wrong.D: The text gives no job for standing still.

MID.stem: What are fast wing players looking for as they run along the sides?
options: A referee to watch
Time to rest
Space near the goal
A way past the pivot
MID.why: The text says wing players run along the sides looking for space near the goal.

wrong.A: The text does not say wing players look for a referee.
wrong.B: Wing players are running fast, not resting.
wrong.D: The pivot is a teammate who opens space for them.

MID.stem: The article talks about a player who gains possession of the ball. What does possession mean here?
options: Having control of it
Throwing it far away
Losing it to a team
Waiting for a turn
MID.why: A player in possession can run, pass, dribble, or shoot, so the player has the ball.

wrong.B: Throwing is one thing a player may do, not what possession means.
wrong.C: Losing possession is the opposite of having it.
wrong.D: The player with the ball is already acting, not waiting.

MID.stem: Why must a team defend fast right after it loses possession?
options: The keeper has left the court
The match is almost over
Its players are too tired
The other team now has the ball
MID.why: When a team loses possession, the other team holds the ball and can attack the goal.

wrong.A: The text does not say the keeper leaves the court.
wrong.B: Losing possession can happen at any time in the match.
wrong.C: Tiredness is not given as a reason.

MID.stem: Why does the author describe wing players, back players, and the pivot?
options: To show who wins each match
To show that players have different jobs
To explain the rules of fouls
To tell how many points goals are worth
MID.why: The author says each team sets its players into roles and then names each role.

wrong.A: The winner is decided by points, not by roles.
wrong.C: Fouls are explained in a different paragraph.
wrong.D: Points are explained near the end of the article.

HIGH.stem: According to the article, how long is each half of a handball match?
options: About thirty minutes
About twenty minutes
About forty-five minutes
About sixty minutes
HIGH.why: The article says a match is split into two equal halves, each about thirty minutes long.

wrong.B: Twenty minutes is not the length given in the text.
wrong.C: Forty-five minutes is not the length given in the text.
wrong.D: Sixty minutes is not the length of one half in the text.

HIGH.stem: A defender grabs an attacker's arm to stop a shot. What will a referee most likely do?
options: Award the attacking team two points
Stop the match for half-time
Call a foul on the defender
Send the keeper off the court
HIGH.why: The article says defenders must never push or hold, because a referee would call a foul.

wrong.A: Every goal counts as one point, and a foul does not give two.
wrong.B: Half-time comes after a set time, not after a foul.
wrong.D: The text does not say the keeper is punished for a defender's foul.

HIGH.stem: In the article, what does the word airborne mean?
options: Standing near the net
Up off the ground
Running along the line
Holding the ball low
HIGH.why: The player has leaped from outside the line, so airborne means up in the air.

wrong.A: The player has jumped, so the player is not standing.
wrong.C: Running is what happens before the leap.
wrong.D: The player leaps high, not low.

HIGH.stem: How are wing players different from back players?
options: Wings guard the keeper, while backs stay by the pivot
Wings are bigger and slower than backs
Wings only defend, while backs only attack
Wings run the sides, while backs shoot from farther out
HIGH.why: Wing players run along the sides near the goal, while back players take hard shots from farther out.

wrong.A: The pivot, not the backs, stands in front of the goal.
wrong.B: The text calls wings quick and backs strong, not slower.
wrong.C: All players must attack and defend, so neither group only does one.
